gap: No result ChatGPT got states the two-year cost including subscriptions: WHOOP 5.0 on its cheapest plan costs $398 over two years (2 × $199), which is more than the Garmin vívoactive 6's one-time $299.99 and about four times the subscription-free Amazfit Helio Strap's $99.99.
standout_why: Android Authority (rank 1) lists only one-time MSRPs. It calls WHOOP 5.0 'subscription-based' but gives no fee and no subscription-inclusive or per-year cost. ChatGPT's own answer gave WHOOP no price at all and just said 'requires an ongoing membership'. I could not open WIRED or Men's Health, the two cited pages: WebFetch said it 'is unable to fetch from' both, and curl was denied. TechRadar and Tom's Guide came back truncated, so the article body never loaded. I can't confirm the cited pages leave the two-year figure out, which is why this is a 2 and not a 3.
decides: This settles which of ChatGPT's picks is cheapest to own. For a man who wants a screenless band for recovery and gym tracking, WHOOP One costs $398 over two years against $99.99 for the Amazfit Helio Strap, which has no required subscription. The cheapest Garmin pick, the vívoactive 6, works out cheaper than WHOOP by the second annual renewal. It also needs about 33 charges a year (365 ÷ 11 days) against WHOOP's 26 (365 ÷ 14). Apple's US store no longer sells the Series 11 that ChatGPT showed. It lists the Series 12 from $399 with up to 24 h battery, which means a charge every day, about 365 a year.
